overview: Doors with depth, doors that lock, doors that swing together, and six variants of every door and four of every trapdoor, for every material in the game.

1.0.6: Wide gates open the way large doors do: their blocks swing out along the leaf.
An open wide gate's leaf is solid, and clicking it shuts the gate.
A wide gate stops against a block where its leaf would land, and comes back from one in its arc.
A row of gates longer than seventeen opens as several gates side by side.
A whole gate is hung at once, and a gate placed against one takes its hinge.
A gate whose gates were hung different ways opens as two leaves.
A gate gone by any means, not only by hand, forgets how it was hung.
A hung gate turned round by a click keeps its leaf on the same post.
Full glass and barred doors have no slats across them, and stacked full glass doors no band at the seams.
1.0.5: A gate standing beside another can be hung left, right or in the middle, like any other gate.
The menu used to offer it nothing but the middle, for a merged wide gate that nothing ever drew.
Hanging a gate sets that gate and the storeys above it, and leaves the gates beside it alone.
1.0.4: Full means full: the glass and barred doors are cut the whole way down.
Stacking two leaves no longer leaves a band of timber across the wall.
A lever opens a double gate as one gate.
Both leaves answer a signal together, the way they already answered a hand.
1.0.3: Autoconnect can straighten a slid door's odd leaf.
One leaf hung the wrong way used to break the whole wall, with no way to put it right.
1.0.2: Doors built out of squares: mega doors, sliding walls and corner hinges.
An autoconnect button joins the leaves for you.
Menus for gates and trapdoors, and a trapdoor that re-hinges on any edge.
Solid doors that keep the light out.
The full glass and barred trapdoors moved to the stonecutter.
1.0.0: Doors that stand proud of the wall instead of lying flat in it.
Doors that lock, and doors that swing together.
The same variants for every wood in the game.
